# dsh-load-agent-rules
English | 中文
Lots of repos already have rules for AI agents, just not in a format DeepSeek Harness reads. Someone
on the team wrote `.cursor/rules/testing.mdc`, another person added `.github/copilot-instructions.m
d`, and there's a `.windsurfrules` from that one month everyone tried Windsurf. DSH reads `AGENTS.md
` and `CLAUDE.md`, but it ignores the rest. So the agent never hears "we use Vitest, not Jest" or "n
ever edit old migrations", even though it's written down right there in the repo.
This plugin finds those rule files and gives them to the model the way each tool meant them to be us
ed. You don't have to convert or copy anything.

That's the `web` profile, the browser UI you start with `dsh web`. If you run DSH another way, use `
headless` (scripts and CI) or `acp` (editor integrations) instead. Each profile keeps its own plugin
list, so add it to every profile you use. It starts working in the next session. Remove it with `ds
h plugin --profile web remove dsh-load-agent-rules`.

## Which files it reads
| Tool | Files |

| Cursor | `.cursor/rules/**/*.mdc` (nested ones in subfolders too), `.cursorrules` |
| GitHub Copil

ot | `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.github/instructions/*.instructions.md` |
| Windsurf | `.wi

ndsurf/rules/*.md`, `.windsurfrules` |
| Cline | `.clinerules` (file or folder) |
| Kiro | `.kiro/st

eering/*.md` |
| Roo Code | `.roo/rules/*`, `.roorules` |
| Gemini CLI | `GEMINI.md` |
| JetBrains J
unie | `.junie/guidelines.md` |
Many repos have the same text under several names, often as a symlink. Duplicates are dropped, and s
o is anything identical to your `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, since DSH already loads those.
## How rules reach the model
Each of those tools has its own idea of when a rule applies. The plugin keeps those meanings instead
of dumping every rule into the prompt.
**Always-on rules** go into context once, at the start of the session. That covers Cursor's `alwaysA
pply: true`, Copilot's main instructions file, Windsurf `always_on`, Kiro `inclusion: always`, and p
lain files like `.cursorrules`. If a rule file changes mid-session, or context compaction drops the
rules, they're sent again.
**File-scoped rules** wait until they're relevant. A Cursor rule with `globs: "*.tsx"`, a Copilot fi
le with `applyTo: "src/db/**"`, a Kiro `fileMatch` or a Windsurf `glob` rule gets attached the first
time the agent reads or edits a matching file. It's attached once, not on every touch. Rules in a n
ested `packages/web/.cursor/rules/` folder only apply inside `packages/web/`.
**Rules with only a description** (Cursor's "agent requested", Windsurf `model_decision`) are listed
by name and description. The model can open any of them with a small `project_rule` tool when it de
cides one is relevant. Manual-only rules show up in that list too.

## Settings
The easy way: open **Plugins** in DSH's sidebar, click **dsh-load-agent-rules**, change what you wan
t and press **Save**. It applies to the next tool call, no restart needed (`toolName` is the one set
ting that still needs a restart, so it is not on the page).
Or add a row like this to `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`, or to `~/.dsh/cordis.patch.y
ml` for every profile. Keys you leave out keep their defaults.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
If your always-on rules go over the budget, the ones that don't fit are listed with a note, and the
model reads them with the tool. Nothing is silently cut.
